subtype: Approach: quit first and figure it out later [Pitfall]
passage:
Parveen was bored at the cooperative office in the kasba, tired of stamping forms she no longer read. One Monday she resigned. "I'll study full time and become a data analyst," she told her friend Jomon at his copy shop. Nobody had asked her how, and she had not asked herself either. She had no savings, no timetable and no course booked.

For three months she watched videos in the afternoon, opened a dozen tabs and finished none. She lay in bed mornings, telling herself she was on a break from thinking. The money in her account thinned to almost nothing.

In month four she took a job at a hardware store just to eat. The data plan was still a sentence in her notebook, only further away than before.

qa.q: Where did Parveen tell Jomon she would study full time?
What was Parveen feeling in the months of drifting, and what shows it?
qa.a: Parveen felt stuck and increasingly anxious, shown by the untouched tabs, the late mornings and the dwindling money.

qa.q: What could Parveen have done before resigning, and why?
qa.a: Parveen could have saved some money and started a course while still working, because a plan and a safety net make the switch less risky.

qa.q: How might Jomon see Parveen's decision to resign?
qa.a: Jomon may have felt supportive but uneasy, having heard a big plan with no steps, and probably wanted to help more.

grounding: Bored at work, the person resigns to study full time with no plan or savings, then takes any job and the switch is delayed.

subtype: Approach: quit first and figure it out later [Pitfall]
passage:
Sami had been bored at the Helsinki insurance office for a year. One grey Monday in February, he resigned. "I'm going to study programming full time," he told his sister Astrid. "I'll figure out the rest."
There was no course picked and not much in the bank.
March he spent trying free tutorials and switching between three languages. April he mostly slept late and watched videos about coding instead of coding. His savings shrank each week, and he stopped buying coffee, then stopped seeing friends.
In May, Astrid came round and found an unopened letter from his landlord on the table. Sami said quietly, "I need a job. Any job."
In June he started at a warehouse, night shifts, stacking boxes. He was too tired to study after work. The programming books sat on the shelf, one bookmark at page thirty.

qa.q: What page was the bookmark on in the programming book?
How was Sami feeling by May, and what shows it?
qa.a: He felt defeated and worried, quietly telling Astrid he needed any job, with an unopened letter from his landlord on the table.

qa.q: What approach would have suited Sami better than resigning first?
qa.a: Choosing one course and studying in the evenings while still employed would have tested the switch without draining his money.

qa.q: How might Astrid feel seeing the unopened letter?
qa.a: Astrid likely felt worried and sad for her brother, realising how far things had slipped since February.

grounding: Shows a bored person resigning to study with no plan or savings, drifting for months, then taking any job and delaying the switch.

subtype: Approach: quit first and figure it out later [Pitfall]
passage:
The public library's reading room in Indore had become Usha's office. She had quit her job at a travel agency in January to prepare for a career in graphic design, with no course, no timetable and little money saved.
Every morning she took the same corner seat, opened a design book, and ended up scrolling job sites or watching tutorials she never finished. Her friend Preeti, a librarian there, noticed she was rarely drawing anything.
By April, Usha was skipping lunch to save money. She asked Preeti if the library needed part-time help. It didn't.
In May she took a job at a call centre, rotating shifts, because it was the first offer. On her last day at the library, she returned the design books, all four renewed three times. Preeti asked when she'd come back. "When I have time," Usha said, not looking at her.

qa.q: Where did Usha take a job in May?
qa.a: She took a job at a call centre, on rotating shifts.

qa.q: How does Usha seem to feel when she says 'When I have time'?
qa.a: She seems discouraged and embarrassed, not looking at Preeti and unsure the switch will happen now.

qa.q: What would you change first in Usha's plan?
qa.a: I would keep the travel agency job while taking one clear design course in the evenings, so there is both income and progress.

qa.q: How does Usha's situation look to Preeti?
qa.a: Preeti sees a friend who comes every day but rarely draws, and likely feels sad watching the plan drift away.

grounding: Shows a person quitting to study with no plan or savings, drifting for months, then taking the first job available and delaying the switch.
